PullRequest.Title: refactor(sessions): move sessions list types and context keys to sessionsListCommon.ts
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Why
`sessionsList.ts` is 11.5k lines, and 23 files import `SessionsGrouping` from it. This is move 1 of phase 2 of splitting it into smaller modules, following the dead-code removal in #349452. Each move is a small move-only PR, so `git blame -C -C` keeps working.

## What changed
- New `sessionsListCommon.ts` with these declarations, byte for byte: the `SessionsGrouping` and `SessionsSorting` enums, the two `MenuId`s, the action and setting IDs, the 33 context keys, and the list item types and type guards.
- The only edits: `export` added to the 6 type guards that `sessionsList.ts` still uses, import lines updated in 42 files (tests included), and the moved blocks deleted. Nothing is re-exported from `sessionsList.ts`.
- `sessionsListCommon.ts` also imports `sessionsList.css` and `disclosure.css`, so the CSS loads at the same point when a module reaches the common module before `sessionsList.ts`.

## Scope
No behavior changes. Things worth changing are left for a later phase.

## Blast Radius
Module load order only. The two `new MenuId(...)` and 33 `new RawContextKey(...)` calls still run once each, the new module does not import `sessionsList.ts`, and there is no import cycle.

## Verification
- Move check (a TypeScript compiler API script): the 257 top-level declaration blocks are identical at base and head, apart from the 6 added `export` keywords. The other 42 files changed only import declarations.
- `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check`, `check-cyclic-dependencies`, and `oxlint` on the 43 changed files all pass.
- Unit tests for the sessions list and its importers: 6,992 tests on base and head.
- Component fixtures `sessionsList`, `sessionsListNotification`, `sessionsInboxScope`, `blockedSessionsList`: 346/346 screenshots identical to base.
- Bundled CSS (desktop, web, server-web, mobile): 6/6 files byte-identical.
- Code OSS Agents window, base and head: every grouping mode, Find, a context menu, drag and drop, and the blocked-sessions list give the same rows. 11 of 12 screenshots are pixel-identical, and the console shows no new errors.

Details in the first comment.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold startup and initialization of sessions configuration, action contributions, and new-chat widgets
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Static dependencies must evaluate before importers initialize. The new common module creates the moved menu identifiers, context keys, enums, and class definition; it does not construct a sessions list or request provider data. NewChatWidget still compares the same grouping enum during focus/background-send decisions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load static dependencies and the existing sessionsList.css/disclosure.css resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional common module; CSS imports resolve to the same resources already imported by sessionsList.ts, not per importer or session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Importers reached sessionsList.ts and its larger dependency graph, including pendingSessions.ts and the same CSS resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Dependency evaluation is on cold initialization; there is no new asynchronous service operation or heavyweight widget creation here.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One module evaluation per module graph/window, independent of session count or the number of importing files. Two newly constructed MenuIds and 33 RawContextKeys replace the identical constructions removed from sessionsList.ts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Normal static module dependency ordering; no new queues, asynchronous task bursts, or per-item initialization.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Module evaluation is shared by importers. RawContextKey metadata and MenuId instances remain single, fixed-size registrations; moved declarations are deleted at the old location. Type-only pendingSessions.ts -> sessionsListCommon.ts import creates no runtime back-edge. The configuration registry's existing reference-counted registration remains unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all changed imports and both sides of the declaration move were inspected; constructor implementations only register fixed-size metadata/identifiers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold-load timing and generated bundle partitioning were not measured or inspected at runtime. No concrete expensive new initialization mechanism was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. This is a declaration extraction with a constant module-loading change, not additional session-scaled work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display, group, sort, search, scroll, and interact with the main sessions list in Agents, editor, and mobile hosts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SessionsView.renderBody creates SessionsList through the existing instantiation path. Refresh reads current sessions and builds the tree synchronously; renderers call the moved, unchanged guards. Visible session rows start lazy provider resolution without awaiting it, so metadata completion is off the immediate rendering critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve metadata for a visible session through the provider controller and, for extension-backed controllers, $resolveChatSessionItem.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one first resolution per distinct rendered resource until invalidation, further joined/cached by the main-thread controller; not one IPC per guard or rerender.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same renderer called observeSession at the same point with the same resource guards and controller caches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Issued without awaiting in renderSession; results update metadata later.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize collapse/expansion state and write grouping, sorting, and layout settings through storageService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing state writes on corresponding user/state changes; collapse-state payload size follows stored sections/resources, not the number of importing modules.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical storage calls, state payloads, and event placement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing synchronous serialization and storage-service invocation; downstream persistence behavior is unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N current sessions, their chats and groups, and V distinct resources entering rendered rows between provider invalidations. The moved guards do the same bounded property/instance checks for each invocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous tree/guard processing with existing animation-frame scheduling. Different visible resources can resolve concurrently; same-resource controller requests join a cached promise. No limiter or scheduling change is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: observeSession uses a resource guard and cached observables. MainThreadChatSessions caches in-flight/resolved promises and removes failed promises. The declaration move neither changes these caches nor their invalidation. Existing next-animation-frame chat-update coalescing and hidden-list suppression remain intact.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced view creation, refresh/update, row rendering, provider dispatch, IPC, and both levels of resolve caching; the diff changes none of these executable paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large-list CPU and provider latency are not measured. Their existing mechanisms and cardinalities are unaffected by this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Type guard bodies, class identity, list construction, row scheduling, serialization, and provider boundaries are preserved.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render automation run history and command-center blocked-session previews
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Automation history and blocked previews still instantiate SessionsFlatList on the same paths. Tree updates and layout precede display; lazy metadata resolution follows the same renderer path as the main list. Import changes only obtain SessionItemStatusContext from its new owner.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Shared session renderer triggers the existing lazy provider metadata resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Distinct rendered resources after history session deduplication and provider resolve caches; not one request for every historical run sharing a session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same SessionsFlatList and SessionItemRenderer implementations handled both products and issued the same cached resolutions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Metadata resolution is not awaited by row rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update DOM dimensions and lay out the flat lists after content-height changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing layout callbacks per list/content-height change; blocked preview height remains bounded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical layout listeners, DOM writes, tree ownership, and disposal paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Layout remains synchronous on preview/history display.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Automation history initially shows 10 runs, deduplicates runs sharing a session, groups adjacent available sessions into flat lists, and increases visibility on Show More. Blocked previews have a height bounded to eight visible rows, while their backing session collection can be larger.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing synchronous rendering/layout; metadata requests may run concurrently across distinct resources and coalesce per resource. The diff does not create additional lists, subscriptions, or asynchronous work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing history group/list reuse, session deduplication, provider metadata caching, and disposal remain unchanged. The moved context key is a module singleton, not allocated per row.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected the flat-list construction sites, history deduplication/visibility cap, blocked-list layout, shared renderer, and disposal ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Existing history size and layout durations vary by user; no diff-introduced growth in their cost or lifetime was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Import splitting does not amplify existing rendering, metadata I/O, or retained list resources.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the New Session from Pull Request picker and resolve context for a selected pull request
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action resolves a repository from existing session observables, then starts repository-scoped PR listing streams. Picker search can await additional pages. The selected PR attachment's resolve callback awaits context retrieval when invoked; this work is separate from initial picker population.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List open PRs and search review-requested/assigned PR groups via GitHub GraphQL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three initial repository-scoped listing streams, then coalesced/sequential open-PR page requests as needed; pages use 100-result sizing. Lower-level pagination can add requests within a stream.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The action had identical repository selection, three initial streams, pagePromise joining, search-generation handling, and result merging.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Network results populate the picker and subsequent searches; no calls occur merely from constructing the moved section context keys.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the selected PR, changed files, issue comments, and review comments.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four concurrently initiated API streams for one selected PR; the three collection streams use 100 items/page and maxPages 100.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same callback invoked the same context fetcher with identical pagination and concurrency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The attachment resolve callback waits for all four streams when requested, not for every PR displayed in the picker.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Combine file patches and map/sort comments into PR context.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One context transformation over the selected PR's returned files/comments.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical patch assembly, comment mapping, and sorting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes before that context resolve returns.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One resolved repository per action invocation, P PR listing pages rather than one repository request per session. Context retrieval scales with files and issue/review comments of the one selected PR.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Three initial listing streams can overlap; open-PR page fetching is single-flight per picker. Selected-context retrieval starts four independent API streams concurrently. Transport-level scheduling is outside the changed code and was not exhaustively traced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Picker pagePromise coalesces concurrent page demands and accumulates already loaded PRs. GitHubApiClient shares account-client acquisition and resets it on invalidation; fetchers show no newly added response cache. Warm and cold response behavior, including failure handling, is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: followed the changed importer through repository resolution, picker grouping/coalescing, service forwarding, GraphQL/REST clients, and context transformation. Only the source of section types/context keys changes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository size, API latency, and lower-level transport pagination/limits affect existing duration; they do not alter PR causality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. No per-session network fan-out, extra context fetch, increased concurrency, or additional serialization is introduced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass against aeda48593263735daaaf7b85b5f77c3d7ff4a48a -> edf724d7879b8f8213f9bd94cdf8b1566f692a37. Inspected the complete 43-file inventory and every diff page (all terminal nextOffset 0). Compared moved declarations with deletions and traced relevant initialization, rendering, caches, lifecycle, IPC, storage serialization, and GitHub network boundaries. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression and no proven historical regression fix qualified for reporting. Static review only; runtime module-load/bundle timing was not measured. The required guide document was requested but the tool exposed only its opening preview because its response exceeded the output limit; learned-regressions guidance was available in full.
